column3: The Hebrew names his soul rather than simply me, and has your mountain with plural possessors.
The Hebrew has a singular bow; BSB has bows.
The Hebrew asks what the righteous has done; BSB asks what he can do.
The Hebrew makes His eyelids the examiners; BSB continues with His eyes.
The Hebrew joins the wicked with the lover of violence as objects of hatred; BSB joins the wicked with the righteous as objects of testing.
The Hebrew names snares and their cup; BSB has fiery coals and omits the cup.
The Hebrew has righteous acts in the plural; BSB says justice.
